annotations.text:
THE OPENING

Name the studio, name the game, and you are in. Two fields.

The roster shows PROSE, never numbers — displayTier() returns 'prose' at research tier 0, so a player reads "Everyone's second favourite" rather than 61. Research turns prose into a band, then a figure. That is the progression tree on the screen the player looks at most.

Starting cash 100,000 against a 147,840 first run: you cannot open without borrowing, and 18 of 24 measured studios survived it.

SET DESIGN — FOUR STEPS

Shape, rarities, cards, print. One wizard, and the sim receives ONE commitment at the end: how much, where, and through whom all lock together, 18 weeks before anything ships.

The rarity screen is the one to look at hardest. A pack holds a fixed number of slots, so setting pull rates DIVIDES them and never adds. And because scarcityExponent is 0.45, a card's contribution to box value scales as pullRate^0.55 — it FALLS as the card gets rarer.

Rarity buys a better story and a worse box. That trade is real arithmetic already in the model, not a rule invented for the UI.

FIVE CARDS, NOT 180

The player crafts the cards that matter; the rest ship as house work at art.houseQuality — which the sim already models, and already gates (sub.houseArtShare reads 0.086).

That is what makes a 180-card set a phone-sized decision.

Aryla appears three times at three rarities — AJ's own example — grouped as a VARIANT RUN. Collectors chase the complete run, which is pull demand, which is the shape chainTerm already models. It would be a third chain kind beside progression and illustration.

THE LOAN IS THE POINT

Measured with a bot that insists on a proper 8,000-box first set whatever the bankroll says, 24 seeds x 20 years:

500k cash   24/24 lived, peak debt 38,790
100k cash   18/24 lived, peak debt 328,842, deaths at year 2.2

DO NOT lower the borrowing ceiling — at 250k, 23 of 24 die.

BLOCKER: the sim borrows AUTOMATICALLY when cash goes negative, so this is not yet a decision. api.borrow is implemented and has never been called by anything — same as api.reprint. Make the explicit loan the normal path and demote auto-borrow to an emergency overdraft.

DIRECTION: DARK, PICKED

All seven screens are now the trade-desk direction — dark ground, monospace throughout, tabular figures. Green is the primary action, amber is information, red is money leaving or a thing not announced.

Left: the light press-room version of the roster, kept for the record. Same data, opposite temperament.

FINISHES ARE PER RARITY

Common and uncommon get nothing. Rare and double rare get holo. The top four get full art, etched, gold foil.

Two budgets now sit on the rarity screen and they are different axes: PACK SLOTS is fixed by physics, FINISHED is a share of the set you choose.

The rule: a finish only works while it is rare. Past a third of the set it stops reading as one, and the print bill climbs faster than the chase does. On the print screen that is a real line — +3,120 on this run, which is 6.5% of the loan.

Card.treatment exists in the model and is read by nothing. This is its consumer.
